title: From trauma reenactment to reciprocal connection in the human–animal bond
abstract: Abstract Background: Judith Herman describes “trauma” as an affliction of the powerless. Research shows that animal trauma similarly reflects helplessness. The parallels between human and animal trauma suggest that the human–animal bond holds significant therapeutic potential – even with animals that have not experienced explicit trauma but live in environments perpetuating helplessness or objectification. These partnerships serve as crucial therapeutic bridges for individuals with impaired human relationships. Case presentation and clinical approach: This case report illustrates key perspectives for fostering partnerships that facilitate relational trauma therapy (also termed “reciprocal therapy”) in the presence of animals. It outlines a novel therapeutic framework for post-trauma intervention that integrates the animal’s lived experiences, aiming to prevent trauma reenactment by strictly rejecting the objectification of one being for the benefit of another. Conclusions: Moving toward relational-reciprocal approaches can create a safe space for mutual emotional and physical healing for both human and animal participants.
